current.title: You'd Guess Indonesia. The Data Says Otherwise.
current.hook: Your guess just got crushed: the US has 165 volcanoes, beating Japan, Russia, Indonesia.
current.closing: Alaska: quietly winning at volcanoes since forever.
current.question: Seen a volcano in person? Where?

segments.say: The US has 165 volcanoes active in 11,700 years; Japan 118, Russia 107, Indonesia 101.
130 of those 165 sit in Alaska alone; without Alaska, the US barely registers.
All four sit on the Ring of Fire, which holds 75% of Earth's volcanoes.

held_for: judge: The story is a strong surprise (the US beats Indonesia, thanks to Alaska), but it is told with a cloned-mascot list, a bar chart, a bubble card and a nonsensical '50% apart' closer.
reasons: judge: The story is a strong surprise (the US beats Indonesia, thanks to Alaska), but it is told with a cloned-mascot list, a bar chart, a bubble card and a nonsensical '50% apart' closer.

judge.one_line: The story is a strong surprise (the US beats Indonesia, thanks to Alaska), but it is told with a cloned-mascot list, a bar chart, a bubble card and a nonsensical '50% apart' closer.
problems: Hook (hook@0.3) is a static ranked list. Data is cloned 5 times as bullets, and nothing shocking hits frame one.
seg1:mid: the map label is cropped to 'Jnited States' and the bar label is truncated to 'United States o...'. Stray cyan circles float over the bars.
seg2:start: the top 40% of the frame is empty, and a single volcano icon floats there with no purpose. Data stands beside the scale instead of loading it.
seg3: '75%'/'25%' in plain bubbles is a bare number card. The 75% text renders garbled as '76%'.
seg4: the closing picture shows '50% apart' (75 minus 25), which is a meaningless derived stat that contradicts the Alaska closing line. Its labels overlap.
Titles say 'Indonesia's Ring of Fire' and 'Indonesia versus Alaska' over scenes that are not about Indonesia.
fixes: Open on the finished shock: a US volcano pile towering over Indonesia's pile, with the hook line on screen from frame one.
Make Data the cause in seg2: he drops each volcano onto the Alaska pan so the beam slams down.
Replace the seg3 bubbles with a ring of fire drawn around the Pacific, where 3 of every 4 volcano markers light up along it.
Rebuild the closer around Alaska: Data lifts Alaska off the US pile, and the count falls from 165 to 35, below Indonesia's 101.
Never print a derived 'X% apart' stat that no line says. Keep labels inside the frame and off each other.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.

PACE: each SAY is ONE spoken sentence of at most 16 words — the number and what it means, nothing else; the HOOK at most 14 words, the CLOSING at most 10, the QUESTION at most 8. A beat is on screen about 8 seconds; a longer line is refused. Each SAY says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
